The main takeaway from our work is that

pilot investigations must be conducted in accordance with the same rigorous standards that are applied to all research, and that the results of pilot investigations should be reported with the same transparency as those of any other research.

pilot studies should not be used to answer the primary questions that will be addressed in subsequent large-scale trials.1-3 Rather, pilot studies should be used to address questions about the feasibility of conducting the larger study, including the feasibility of recruitment, retention, adherence, and data collection; to inform decisions regarding sample size; to identify and refine the intervention, including the optimal delivery method and dose and the most appropriate outcome measures; and to identify and resolve potential barriers to conducting the larger trial.1-
pilot studies should be conducted in a way that allows the investigator to answer the primary research questions of interest and to inform decisions about the feasibility of the larger study.
